title: Foreign Key
body:
A column holding the [[Primary Key]] value of a row in another table — a note on one shelf's item pointing to an item on another shelf. `reviews.product_id` holding a value from `products.id` is what records "this review belongs to that product".

This is the feature that makes a relational database *relational*, and it's what a [[JOIN]] traverses. Declaring it as a real constraint rather than just a convention buys **referential integrity**: the database engine itself refuses to insert a review pointing at a product that doesn't exist, and refuses (or cascades) a delete that would orphan rows. That enforcement lives on the database server, not in application code, which is precisely the point — it holds even when a buggy script or a manual query gets it wrong. See [[SQL]].
